question: Under the legacy Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, what four categories does the examiner score?
choice_a: Speed, braking, signaling, and lane position
choice_b: Turns, intersections, curves, and railroad crossings
choice_c: Encroachments, pull-ups, outside vehicle observations (looks), and final position
choice_d: Clutch usage, gear usage, brake usage, and steering
explanation: Section 12.1 lists encroachments, pull-ups, outside vehicle observations (looks), and final position as the four scored categories on the legacy skills test.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.1 — Scoring

question: According to Section 12.1, what counts as an "encroachment" during the Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test?
choice_b: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of the vehicle
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
choice_d: Finishing an exercise in the wrong final position
explanation: The examiner scores the number of times you touch or cross over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of your vehicle as an encroachment.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.1 — Scoring

question: Which of the following does NOT count as a "pull-up" under Section 12.1 scoring rules?
choice_a: Pulling forward to clear an encroachment
choice_b: Pulling forward to get a better position
choice_c: Pulling forward after crossing a boundary line
explanation: The manual specifically states that stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up; only pulling forward to clear an encroachment or gain a better position does.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.1 — Scoring

question: Before exiting the vehicle to perform an outside vehicle observation ("look") during the legacy Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s)
choice_c: Sound the horn twice
explanation: Section 12.1 requires the driver to place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s) before exiting to check the vehicle's external position.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.1 — Scoring

question: How many points of contact must a driver maintain with the vehicle when safely exiting to perform an outside observation (non-bus)?
choice_c: Three
explanation: The driver must exit by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact with the vehicle at all times.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.1 — Scoring

question: Under the legacy Section 12 scoring rules, how does the maximum number of looks allowed on Straight Line Backing compare to other exercises?
choice_a: Two looks, same as other exercises
choice_b: One look, one fewer than the two allowed on other exercises
choice_c: Three looks, one more than other exercises
explanation: The maximum is generally two looks, except Straight Line Backing, which allows only one look.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.1 — Scoring

question: In the legacy Section 12.2.1 Straight Line Backing exercise, what must the driver avoid while backing?
choice_c: Looking in mirrors
choice_d: Touching or crossing over the exercise boundaries between two rows of cones
explanation: The driver must back the vehicle in a straight line between two rows of cones without touching or crossing over the exercise boundaries.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.2.1 — Straight Line Backing

question: In Section 12.2.2 Offset Back/Right, where is the target parking space located relative to the vehicle?
choice_a: To the right rear of the vehicle
choice_c: To the left rear of the vehicle
explanation: The driver backs into a space that is to the right rear of the vehicle without striking the side or rear boundaries.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.2.2 — Offset Back/Right

question: In the legacy Section 12.2.4 Parallel Park (Driver Side) exercise, on which side is the parking space located?
choice_c: Directly behind
explanation: The manual states you may be asked to park in a parallel parking space that is on your left for this exercise.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.2.4 — Parallel Park (Driver Side)

question: What does the legacy Section 12.2.6 Alley Dock exercise require the driver to do?
choice_a: Drive forward through an alley and stop within a marked box
choice_b: Parallel park on the right side of the street
choice_c: Back in a straight line between two rows of cones
choice_d: Sight-side back the vehicle into an alley so the entire vehicle is straight with the alley
explanation: The driver must sight-side back the vehicle completely into the alley with the entire vehicle straight with the alley, without going beyond the boundary.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.2.6 — Alley Dock

question: What are the four exercises included in North Dakota's modernized Basic Control Skills Test (Section 12M)?
choice_a: Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, Reverse Offset Backing
choice_b: Straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, alley dock
choice_c: Parallel park driver side, parallel park conventional, alley dock, straight line backing
explanation: Section 12M lists Step 1 Forward Stop, Step 2 Straight-Line Backing, Step 3 Forward Offset Tracking, and Step 4 Reverse Offset Backing as the exercises.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12M — Basic Control Skills Test Exercises

question: Under Section 12M, points are awarded or deducted for which of the following?
choice_a: Speed, mirror usage, and turn signal timing
choice_b: Changing direction to gain a better position, crossing/touching boundary lines or cones, and final position
choice_c: Clutch usage and gear usage only
explanation: The manual states you receive points for changing direction to gain a better position, crossing over or touching boundary lines or cones, and for your final position.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12M — Basic Control Skills Test

question: Under Section 12.1M, which vehicle part touching a boundary line or cone does NOT count as an encroachment?
choice_c: The vehicle's mirrors, or unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height (such as a bucket truck)
explanation: Encroachments exclude the vehicle's mirrors and unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height (like a bucket truck); unique parts below that height are counted as encroachments.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.1M — Scoring

question: On which two exercises are pull-ups scored under Section 12.1M?
choice_c: Exercise 1 and Exercise 4
choice_d: Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
explanation: Pull-ups apply to Exercise 2 Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 Reverse Offset Backing, where the examiner scores the number of times you pull up.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.1M — Scoring

question: Under Section 12.1M, how many free looks are allowed on Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) versus Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)?
choice_a: One free look on Exercise 2, two free looks on Exercise 4
choice_b: Two free looks on Exercise 2, one free look on Exercise 4
choice_c: One free look on both
explanation: The manual allows a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2 Straight-Line Backing and two free looks on Exercise 4 Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.1M — Scoring

question: Under Section 12.1M, final vehicle position is scored on which exercises?
choice_c: Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for final vehicle position on Exercise 2 Straight-Line Backing and on Exercise 4 Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.1M — Scoring

question: Under Section 12.1M, what happens if a driver opens the vehicle door while the vehicle is still moving (not in neutral/park)?
choice_b: It may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_c: It is simply noted but not penalized
explanation: Opening the door while the vehicle is moving, rather than in neutral and park, may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.1M — Scoring

question: Under Section 12.2M, what must a driver do upon completing an exercise to inform the examiner?
choice_c: Roll down the window and state "done"
choice_d: Set the parking brake, shift to neutral/park, and sound the horn
explanation: Upon completing an exercise, the driver must set the parking brake, shift to neutral/park, and sound the horn to inform the examiner the exercise is complete.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.2M — Exercises

question: In Exercise 1 (Forward Stop) of the modernized test, how many times may the driver stop?
choice_c: As many times as needed
explanation: The driver must drive forward through the alley and stop with the front-most part of the vehicle within the box, and may stop only once.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.2M — Exercise 1, Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) of the modernized test, how many free pull-ups are allowed and how many times may the driver exit the vehicle to check?
choice_c: One free pull-up, exit only once
explanation: The driver is allowed one free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one time to check around the vehicle during this exercise.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.2M — Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing

question: What is unique about Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking) compared to the other modernized exercises?
choice_a: The driver may stop and back up as needed
choice_b: The driver must complete it entirely in reverse
choice_c: The driver is not scored for encroachments
choice_d: The driver must maneuver forward without stopping, and stopping ends the exercise
explanation: The driver is not allowed to stop, back up, or exit the vehicle during Exercise 3; if the driver stops, the exercise is ended.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.2M — Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking), which direction does the driver steer through the opening into the opposite lane?
choice_c: Straight only
explanation: The driver drives forward and steers to the left through the opening into the opposite lane, keeping the right-most rear tire between the cone and the line.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.2M — Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing), within how many feet of the rear of the alley must the driver bring the rear of the vehicle?
choice_c: Five feet
explanation: The driver must offset back into the alley, bringing the rear-most part of the vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.2M — Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits ("looks") are allowed during Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)?
choice_c: Two free pull-ups, two exits
explanation: The driver is allowed two free pull-ups and may exit the vehicle a maximum of two times to check around the vehicle during this exercise.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 12.2M — Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing

question: What must a CDL applicant do throughout the on-road driving test in North Dakota?
choice_a: Wear a seat belt, obey all traffic signs/signals/laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation
choice_b: Exceed the speed limit only when passing
choice_c: Turn off the seat belt reminder chime
choice_d: Complete the route in under 15 minutes
explanation: Section 13.1 requires the driver to wear a seat belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1 — How You Will Be Tested

question: If the test route does not include a certain traffic situation, what will the examiner do?
choice_b: Ask the applicant to simulate it by describing what they would do
choice_c: Extend the test route until the situation occurs
choice_d: Skip that scoring category entirely with no discussion
explanation: If the test route lacks certain traffic situations, the applicant may be asked to simulate it by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing in that situation.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1 — How You Will Be Tested

question: According to Section 13.1.1, when is coasting considered "unsafe" while approaching a turn?
choice_a: Whenever the driver removes their foot from the accelerator
choice_c: When the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
explanation: Unsafe coasting occurs when the vehicle is out of gear, with the clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral, for more than the length of the vehicle.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.1 — Turns

question: If stopping behind another vehicle before a turn, where should the driver stop?
choice_a: Bumper to bumper for a tight gap
choice_b: At least one full block behind
choice_c: Directly beside the vehicle ahead
choice_d: Where the rear tires of the vehicle ahead are visible, maintaining a safe gap
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop where they can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead, maintaining a safe gap.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.1 — Turns

question: What must a driver's vehicle NOT do while stopped at an intersection, per Section 13.1.2?
choice_c: Use the turn signal
explanation: Section 13.1.2 states that the vehicle must not roll forward or backward while stopped at an intersection.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.2 — Intersections

question: While driving through an intersection, what should the driver avoid doing, per Section 13.1.2?
choice_b: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_c: Keeping hands on the wheel
explanation: The manual instructs drivers not to change lanes while proceeding through an intersection.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.2 — Intersections

question: During the urban business portion of the on-road test (Section 13.1.3), where should the vehicle be centered?
choice_c: In the proper lane, generally the right-most lane
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should be centered in the proper lane, the right-most lane, while keeping up with the flow of traffic without exceeding the posted speed limit.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.3 — Urban Business

question: During the multiple-lane portion of the test (Section 13.1.4), which lane change sequence is the driver asked to perform?
choice_c: A U-turn maneuver
choice_d: Left, then back to the right
explanation: During multiple lane portions of the test, the driver is asked to change lanes to the left, and then back to the right, using proper traffic checks and signals.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.4 — Lane Changes

question: Once on the expressway, per Section 13.1.5, what must the driver maintain?
choice_a: Proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed
choice_b: Maximum legal speed at all times
choice_c: A position in the left-most lane only
choice_d: Constant lane changes to pass slower traffic
explanation: Once on the expressway, the driver must maintain proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed while continuing to check traffic.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.5 — Expressway or Limited Access Highway

question: When exiting the expressway, per Section 13.1.5, the driver must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain what?
choice_a: Radio volume at a safe level
choice_b: Adequate spacing between the vehicle and other vehicles
choice_c: A constant speed matching the highway
choice_d: A following distance of exactly one car length
explanation: Once on the exit ramp, the driver must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between the vehicle and other vehicles.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.5 — Expressway or Limited Access Highway

question: Before executing the Stop/Start maneuver, what turn signal should the driver activate while preparing to pull to the side of the road?
choice_c: Right turn signal
explanation: As the driver prepares for the Stop/Start maneuver, the manual instructs them to check traffic and activate the right turn signal.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.6 — Stop/Start

question: Once stopped for the Stop/Start maneuver, per Section 13.1.6, what should the driver do with the parking brake and gear shift?
choice_a: Leave the parking brake off and stay in drive
choice_b: Apply the parking brake but keep the vehicle in gear
choice_c: Leave the vehicle running in reverse
choice_d: Apply the parking brake and move the gear shift to neutral or park
explanation: Once stopped, the driver must apply the parking brake and move the gear shift to neutral or park, then remove their feet from the brake and clutch pedals.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.6 — Stop/Start

question: When instructed to resume after the Stop/Start maneuver, which turn signal should the driver activate?
choice_c: No turn signal, only four-way flashers
explanation: When instructed to resume, the driver must turn off the four-way flashers and activate the left turn signal before pulling back into traffic.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.6 — Stop/Start

question: Per Section 13.1.7, when should a driver reduce speed for a curve?
choice_b: Before entering the curve, so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_c: Only after completing the curve
choice_d: Speed reduction is not necessary for curves
explanation: Before entering a curve, the driver should reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required while in the curve.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.7 — Curve

question: Per Section 13.1.8, what is a commercial driver prohibited from doing while any part of the vehicle is in a railroad crossing?
choice_c: Stopping, changing gears, passing another vehicle, or changing lanes
explanation: The manual states a driver must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.8 — Railroad Crossing

question: For a bus, school bus, or vehicle displaying placards, Section 13.1.8 requires stopping within how many feet of the nearest rail, but not less than how many feet?
choice_a: Within 100 feet, not less than 25 feet
choice_b: Within 30 feet, not less than 5 feet
choice_c: Within 75 feet, not less than 20 feet
choice_d: Within 50 feet, not less than 15 feet
explanation: The manual requires stopping the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail before a railroad crossing.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.8 — Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass during the on-road test, what might the examiner ask the driver to identify, per Section 13.1.9?
choice_c: The number of lanes
explanation: After driving under an overpass, the driver may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.9 — Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: After going over a bridge, what might the examiner ask the driver to state, per Section 13.1.9?
choice_c: The bridge's official name
explanation: After going over a bridge, the driver may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted weight limit was.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.9 — Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: Per Section 13.1.10, how far away from students must a school bus come to a complete stop for a student discharge?
choice_c: At least 10 feet
explanation: The driver must bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.10 — Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: While approaching a student pickup for discharge, per Section 13.1.10, what warning devices should the driver activate?
choice_b: Hazard flashers and the left turn signal
choice_c: Red warning lights and the stop arm
choice_d: Amber warning lights and the right turn signal
explanation: As the driver approaches the student pickup, they must activate amber warning lights and the right turn signal while moving as far right as possible.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.10 — Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: Under Section 13.1.11 General Driving Behavior, which of the following is a scored clutch usage violation?
choice_a: Riding the clutch to control speed or "popping" the clutch
choice_b: Using the clutch to shift when needed
choice_c: Double-clutching when shifting
explanation: The manual identifies riding the clutch to control speed, coasting with the clutch depressed, or "popping" the clutch as improper clutch usage.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.11 — General Driving Behavior

question: Per Section 13.1.11, when shifting near railroad tracks, what must be true before shifting?
choice_a: The driver must be in neutral the whole time
choice_b: Both the power unit and trailer(s) must have cleared the tracks
choice_c: The vehicle must be at a complete stop
choice_d: The four-way flashers must be on
explanation: The manual states a driver should not shift on railroad tracks and must be sure both the power unit and trailer(s) have cleared the tracks before shifting.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.11 — General Driving Behavior

question: Per Section 13.1.11, on a multiple-lane road, in which lane should a driver finish a left turn?
choice_c: The lane directly to the right of the center line
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should finish a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line on a multiple lane road.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.11 — General Driving Behavior

question: Per Section 13.1.11, when should a driver cancel their turn signal?
choice_b: Only when another driver flashes their lights
choice_c: Turn signals should never be cancelled manually
choice_d: After completion of the turn or lane change
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to cancel turn signals upon completion of a turn or lane change.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 13.1.11 — General Driving Behavior
